cohort: 88,837 pregnant women in their first pregnancy from the Malaysian National Obstetrics and Gynaecology Registry (2010-2012)
finding: This retrospective cohort study of 88,837 first-time pregnant women in Malaysia found that using the lower BMI thresholds recommended for Asian populations by the WHO was a more sensitive predictor of adverse obstetric outcomes.
mod_finding: Higher BMI in first pregnancy was associated with increased risk of cesarean section.
